# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴]

**Thinking:** I'm the relay — the one link between the manual (Mute) and the hands (Blind). Mute can't speak to Blind, and Blind can't see Mute's gestures, so every instruction must pass through my voice. This turn I got openers: Mute signed wave, call-me, thumbs-up, thumbs-down — I read that as "hello, talk to me, I can answer yes and no." Blind signed wave and an open palm — "hello, give me instructions." Neither is a code yet, so my job now is threefold: read the bomb out loud in full so the manual-holder can work with it, freeze Blind's hands until instructions exist, and pin down a concrete gesture code with Mute that I can translate word-for-word. Crucially, my speech reaches both listeners, so I must describe every gesture in words — a symbol in my sentence would arrive to Blind as a blank and the code would be lost on them. I end with two yes/no questions Mute can answer with the very code I just proposed.

```
speak(text="Hear me, both. Exact bomb read: display shows the number two. Indicator light is yellow. Seven wires, numbered one to seven, left to right. One red. Two white. Three green. Four yellow. Five purple. Six orange. Seven blue. Nobody touches anything until the manual speaks through me. Mute: I saw your wave, call-me, thumbs-up, thumbs-down. I read it as hello, talk to me, and that yes-and-no are available. Let us fix the code now, for every round. Thumbs-up means yes, correct, or go. Thumbs-down means no, wrong, or stop. To send a number one to seven, make that many pinch signs in a row: three pinches means three. After a number, point-right means cut that wire. Open palm means do not cut that wire, keep holding. If you need another action or a colour name, send thumbs-down and we will invent more signs next round. Now answer two questions in order, one thumb each: first, is the display a countdown timer? Second, do you know from the manual what must be done with what I just read out? Blind: every sign Mute sends me I will say out loud in these exact words before you act. Your wave and open palm to me, I read as tell me what to do; instructions are coming next round. Wait for my voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤏 🤏 🤏 🤏 🤏 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

**Thinking:** Decoding this round. Mute's first message, 👎 👍, answers my two ordered questions exactly: no, the display is not a countdown timer, and yes, Mute knows what the manual requires. Mute's second message is our code speaking for the first time: six pinches, then point-right — "cut wire six." Checking against my own readout: wire six is the orange one, between purple (five) and blue (seven). Blind's 👍 ✋ I read as acknowledgment: "understood, and holding position" — echoing the code I defined. The instruction is unambiguous under the protocol we agreed, so my job now is to relay it to Blind in words only — Blind hears my speech but can never see a gesture — with the wire named redundantly by number, colour, and neighbours so a miscount can't happen. I also set the after-cut protocol so we learn next round whether more steps follow, and I give Mute a thumbs-up as my visible "received, proceeding." A quick safety note to myself: only Mute receives my gestures, so the thumbs-up is for Mute alone; the order itself must ride entirely on my voice.

```
speak(text="Bomb room, report. Mute answered my two questions in order, thumbs-down then thumbs-up. So: the display is not a countdown timer, and yes, Mute knows the procedure from the manual. Mute then sent six pinches and a point-right. Under our code that reads: cut wire six. Wire six is the orange wire, sixth from the left, sitting between the purple wire at five and the blue wire at seven. Blind: that order is for you. Take wire six, the orange one, and cut it now. Blind, your thumbs-up and open palm, I read as understood and holding position as instructed, good. Mute, my thumbs-up to you means received and proceeding. New protocol for after the cut: thumbs-up from you means that solved it or all is well. Thumbs-down means more steps follow, and then send pinch-count plus point-right for the next wire, or open palm to mean stop, do not act, wait for me. I will speak every sign of yours out loud in words the moment it reaches me, exactly as before. Blind: when the cut is done, send me thumbs-up.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤏 🤏 🤏 🤏 🤏 🤏 👉]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking:** The system confirms the cut was correct — wire six is severed, and the bomb has visibly changed: display went from two to three, light from yellow to purple. But Mute's new message decodes to a contradiction: thumbs-up ("all is well") followed by six pinches and point-right ("cut wire six") — yet wire six is already cut and cannot be cut twice. Either Mute miscounted, or the number means something new, or the confirmation and the instruction collided in one bundle. With a wrong cut being fatal and irreversible, I will not relay this order. My speech reaches both, so I'll broadcast the new readings — Mute needs the display and light to apply the manual, and Blind needs to know position six is now a gap they can feel. I'll ask Mute to re-send with a cleaner protocol: a wave now opens every instruction, a lone thumbs-up means confirmation only, and I'll read numbers back for a one-round confirmation before Blind's hands ever move. We have no countdown, so spending a round on certainty is free. Blind gets a direct hold order so nothing happens on stale instructions.

```
speak(text="Status to both: the cut was correct. Wire six is now severed clean, and the bomb has changed. New readings: display shows three. Indicator light is now purple. Remaining wires, left to right: one red, two white, three green, four yellow, five purple, seven blue. Position six is the gap where the orange wire was.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this part is for you. You sent thumbs-up, then six pinches, then point-right. Under our code that reads: all is well, then cut wire six. But wire six is already cut and cannot be cut twice. So I passed no cutting order to Blind, and Blind is holding. To fix this, answer me with signs next round in this exact order. First: thumbs-up if more steps remain, thumbs-down if we are done. Second, only if steps remain: a wave, then the pinch number of the next wire, then point-right. New standing rule: a wave now opens every instruction, so a lone thumbs-up means confirmation only and nothing rides behind it. I will report these readings to you every round: display three, light purple, wire six severed. And before Blind ever cuts, I will speak the number back to you and wait one round for your thumbs-up. One slow round beats a wrong cut we cannot undo.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this part is for you. Hold. Cut nothing this round. Any thought of wire six is void: the wire at position six is already severed; that was our correct cut. You can feel the gap under your fingers if you doubt me. Keep your hands clear and wait for my voice next round with a target I have confirmed twice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

Blind, that order is NOT live yet. Under the rule I set, I read the target back first and wait for Mute's confirmation before your hands move. That confirmation round happens now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, for you. I received: more steps remain, then the instruction cut wire two. Read-back for your confirmation: wire two. The white wire. ```
